questions.text: What does a PatchGAN discriminator primarily assess in Pix2Pix?

options.A: Whether translating an image to another domain and back reproduces the input.
options.B: Whether the generator assigns an exact normalized probability to the whole image.
options.C: Whether local image patches look realistic, using a grid of discriminator scores.
options.D: Whether every generated pixel exactly equals its paired target pixel.

questions.explanation: PatchGAN produces scores for local receptive fields rather than only one whole-image score. In Pix2Pix it sees the condition/output pair; cycle consistency and exact pixel reconstruction are separate objectives, not its patch-realism test.

questions.text: A paired sketch-to-photo model produces realistic photos that often ignore the input sketch. You discover its discriminator sees only the output photo. Which change directly lets the discriminator assess input-output consistency?

options.A: Feed the discriminator the sketch and candidate photo together.
options.B: Remove the sketch from the generator input as well.
options.C: Replace each paired target with a randomly chosen real photo.
options.D: Evaluate only the realism of pooled generated photos.

questions.explanation: A conditional discriminator D(x, y) sees both the input sketch and output photo, so it can assess their correspondence as well as realism. A discriminator seeing only y cannot directly inspect consistency with x.

questions.text: This toy CycleGAN check computes round-trip error. What does it print?
questions.code:
def G(x):
    return x + 3

def F(y):
    return y - 2

x = 4
y = G(x)
x_reconstructed = F(y)
cycle_error = abs(x_reconstructed - x)
print(y, x_reconstructed, cycle_error)
questions.explanation: G(4) = 7, then F(7) = 5. The round-trip error is abs(5 - 4) = 1. Cycle consistency penalizes failure to reconstruct the source after translating in both directions.
